notes: No fixed file, directory, or top-k candidate cap is used.
The nine frozen diagnostic tasks and three pinned repository revisions are unchanged from V3.
The semantic lexical arm preserves broad V2 alias expansion as a control.
The only retrieval change from V3 is to recognize complete known concepts such as WebSocket before splitting unrecognized CamelCase tokens.

Concept-weighted retrieval counts each narrow alias group once, weights filename and directory-segment matches, and qualifies candidates by two distinct concepts, one concept found in at most 2% of enumerated paths, or a filename match with weighted score at least 2.0.
The stable selection control calculates its 1% guard from the complete enumerated repository population.
Provenance rescue keeps the 0.65 absolute threshold and rescues scores at or above 0.50 only when a rare path concept or filename concept supports the match; it has no repository-wide fallback.
The weighted stable and rescue arms share exact file-scoring batches; the selection comparison adds no model calls.
All arms use four concurrent independent System One requests and the shared SystemOneClient transport.
The weighted arm must recover all 9 primary targets and reduce OpenClaw mean scored files below 2,000 to pass the operational gate.
Single-repeat diagnostic comparison; primary labels are incomplete for supporting files and do not establish fresh-task generalization.
